newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-BLUE JAYS SIGN RUBEN SIERRA TO MINOR-LEAGUE PACT.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-BLUE JAYS SIGN RUBEN SIERRA TO MINOR-LEAGUE PACT.

text.p: The Toronto Blue Jays, hoping to add punch to the American League's lightest-hitting team, signed veteran outfielder Ruben Sierra to a minor-league contract Sunday and assigned him to Triple-A Syracuse.
The move came four days after Sierra was released by the Cincinnati Reds.

The 31-year-old switch-hitter had just two homers and seven RBI in 25 games for the Reds while batting just .244. Cincinnati acquired him from Detroit last October for two minor-leaguers but assumed just $600,000 of Sierra's $6.5 million salary for 1997.

Sierra's last productive season was 1995, when he combined to hit .263 with 19 homers and 86 RBI in 126 games for the Oakland Athletics and New York Yankees. Last year, he batted just .247 for the Yankees and Tigers with 12 homers and 72 RBI.
The Blue Jays are last in the American League with a .239 team batting average and their 128 runs are 16 fewer than any other team in the league.
